step_by_step_reasoning: The Nielsen Marketing Cloud 'DataOut' architecture processes high-volume marketing segmentation data (up to 250 billion events per day) and delivers it to over 100 partner ad networks. First, incoming file notifications enter via an Ingest SQS queue to an Ingest Manager Lambda, which registers metadata in a Postgres RDS database. A Work Manager Lambda reads pending file metadata from RDS and triggers an EMR Spark cluster to transform the data, reading raw files from an input S3 bucket and saving formatted files to an output S3 bucket, while reporting job status back to RDS. Next, a Fan-out Work Manager Lambda queries RDS for files ready to be uploaded, applying rate limiting controls before invoking worker Lambdas concurrently. Worker Lambdas read transformed data from the output S3 bucket and upload payloads to external Ad Networks. To prevent database connection bottlenecks, Worker Lambdas send completion/retry statuses to an SQS Status Queue, which is batch-consumed by a Status Updater Lambda to perform batch updates back into the Postgres RDS database.

graph.categories: Data Lake, Serverless, Data Ingestion, AdTech
graph.notes: Handles 250B events/day with 55TB peak volume, 17M files, and up to 3,000 concurrent Lambda instances. Employs rate limiting per network (e.g., Mbps, HTTP connection counts) and batch queue updates to avoid Postgres RDS connection choking.
